messages.subject: Problem with the probability of detection
parts:
Good morning everyone,

I have a problem in the Distance program, because when running the analyzes the Expected values are all the same and in the graph indicating the Detection probability the red line is presented as a line starting from number 1. I have a dataset with several species. and this problem has appeared for some and not others.
Can anyone tell what may have happened and how to fix it? Could it be something wrong when importing data into the program?

Forgive me for typo or consistency, because I am Brazilian and translate the text with google translator.

Thanks in advance for your help.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Problem with the probability of detection
parts:
Renan

Thanks for supplying the chi-square goodness of fit table, that helps.   You will notice that in the last distance band (85.7 to 100) you have the second greatest number of detections.  In other words, detectability does not appear to be diminishing as a function of distance for this data set.

Distance sampling assumes that detection probability is a non-increasing function of distance.  If detection probability is high at great distances, then it must also be high at small distances.  Consequently, the Distance software has fit a uniform detection function as best for these data.  This has a horizontal line for a detection function and the same expected values in your chi-square table for all of your distance bands.

I fear the difficulty lies with your data and perhaps field methods for this species.
